title: Genitem: A User-friendly Tool for the Generation and Pre-validation of Items with AI
description:
Genitem (Jan et al., 2026) is a free, browser-based suite that helps researchers build, adapt and check questionnaires, surveys and measurement scales with generative AI, while keeping human expertise in charge. All language models run locally on the researcher's own computer through Ollama (Windows, macOS or Linux). No item, response or personal data is sent to an external service, which makes Genitem suitable for studies with strict ethical or data-protection requirements.

Its core tool, Item generation, works in two stages. First, a configurator coordinates AI agents organised in a hierarchy. The researcher chooses the model and defines the role of each agent. For example, a generator agent drafts a set of items on a given construct, then several reviewer agents (typically three to eight) independently check that the items stay on topic, follow item-writing rules and are free from ethical bias. This review cycle is repeated several times, each agent taking the others' feedback into account, before a final agent compiles the items into a pool. Second, the AI-GENIE R package (Russell-Lasalandra et al., 2026) analyses this pool with network psychometrics, removes redundant or unstable items and retains the most stable ones. When several constructs are measured, the researcher first assigns each item to its factor.

Around this core, Genitem offers tools in three groups. Build and adapt: item generation, new items, questionnaire review and back-translation. Check before data collection: psychometric quality, item sorting, condition variation and model testing. Analyse text responses: open-ended response coding, textometrics and verbatims, which compares AI and human coding.

Genitem's strength lies in making the technical side simple and easy to understand, while giving human judgement the leading role in directing the AI agents. The interface is available in English, French, Spanish, German, Portuguese and Italian.

This archive contains the presentation of the tools in six languages (English, French, Spanish, German, Portuguese and Italian, the last four translated with AI), links to the introductory videos with their thumbnails, and the two R scripts used for the AI-GENIE analysis (single and multiple constructs). The tools themselves are used from the website: https://genitem.recherche-formation.com.

Reference: Russell-Lasalandra, L. L., Christensen, A. P., & Golino, H. (2026). Generative psychometrics via AI-GENIE: Automatic item generation and validation with network-integrated evaluation. Behavior Research Methods, 58(8), 217. https://doi.org/10.3758/s13428-026-03082-1
notes: Carried out within a project affiliated with the University of Fribourg, supported by the Centenary Fund (project FC-26-989), in collaboration with the Université de Montréal. Contact: info@genitem.education
